column3: The Hebrew presents this as an independent statement and uses singular people; BSB begins though and uses them.
The Hebrew uses singular references and makes the LORD the active subject not condemning; BSB describes not letting them be condemned.
The Hebrew does not explicitly supply tree in its native growth comparison as BSB does.
The Hebrew names an after-end for a man of peace; BSB interprets it as posterity.
The Hebrew has completed passive verbs; BSB has future verbs.
The Hebrew does not explicitly supply He is before their stronghold as BSB does.
The Hebrew moves from completed help and deliverance to uncompleted verbs and ends with completed refuge-taking; BSB uses present verbs throughout.
